hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions: real product, schedules (product fault)
hard_gates.evidence: POST /api/jobs/schedules (ScheduleEndpoints.Create) checks only that the kind is schedulable. It never checks the kind's own run permission, even though the endpoint's summary says 'Add a schedule for a kind of job the caller may run'. Start and Rerun do check it. Live demo (attack/planner.mjs, planner.txt): a user whose role holds only jobs.schedules.create and jobs.schedules.read got 403 on POST /api/jobs/jobs {type:'jobs.cleanup'} (the clean-up kind's run permission is jobs.schedules.update) and 403 on GET /api/jobs/jobs. The same user got 201 on POST /api/jobs/schedules {type:'jobs.cleanup', cron:'* * * * *', payload:{retentionDays:30}}. Within a minute the worker queued the job as system work and ran it: result {deleted: 50038}, and the workspace's job total fell from 100,014 to 49,977. Audit (attack/planner-audit.txt): 50,038 deletes recorded with actor_kind 'job' and no actor. Reproduced in a gate-style test on the unplanted code (plants/CriticProofP2.cs test 2, unplanted-proof.log: start 403, kinds 403, schedule 201). No gate or module test caught it. The screen offers this user no kind (11-planner-screen-offers-no-kind.jpg), so only the server check is missing.

biggest_gap.title: A user who may only add schedules can run any schedulable job kind as system work, including ones whose run permission they lack
biggest_gap.detail: ScheduleEndpoints.Create (src/Modules/Jobs/Erp.Modules.Jobs/Schedules/ScheduleEndpoints.cs) checks only `type is { Schedulable: true }`. It never checks the kind's RunPermission, while JobEndpoints.Start and Rerun do. Update has the same hole: a jobs.schedules.update holder can re-enable a self-check schedule or change its parameters without jobs.jobs.run. The scheduler then queues the job as system work with no requesting user, so jobs.schedules.create is in effect permission to run every schedulable kind. Today that kind list includes the clean-up, which deletes job history. Later it will include whatever schedulable jobs other modules add, such as payroll runs, period closing or bulk postings, which a UAE trading or manufacturing company would guard with their own permissions. The audit trail records the deletions as done by 'job' with no actor. The fix: in Create, refuse a kind whose RunPermission the caller lacks (and in Update when it enables a schedule or changes its parameters), report Schedulable in GET /types the same way, and add a p12 gate that, for each schedulable kind, gives exactly jobs.schedules.create and requires a 403. That gate should also cover per-kind rerun, because plant P2 shows the per-kind check on rerun is untested too.
biggest_gap.evidence: To reproduce on the demo: as admin, create a role with permissions ['jobs.schedules.create','jobs.schedules.read'] and a user with it. As that user, POST /api/jobs/jobs {type:'jobs.cleanup',payload:{retentionDays:30}} answers 403, and POST /api/jobs/schedules {scheduleName:'x',type:'jobs.cleanup',cron:'* * * * *',payload:{retentionDays:30}} answers 201. A minute later GET /api/jobs/schedules/{id} names lastJobId, and that job ended 'succeeded' with source 'scheduler' and result {deleted:50038}; the job total fell from 100,014 to 49,977. Script and output: gauntlet/evidence/p12-jobs/r2/attack/planner.mjs and planner.txt, audit rows in attack/planner-audit.txt. Gate-style reproduction on the unplanted code: plants/CriticProofP2.cs, test A_user_who_may_only_add_schedules_schedules_a_kind_he_may_not_run (unplanted-proof.log: start 403, kinds 403, schedule 201).

other_findings: Rule 5 (Arabic): the jobs list's main column shows the English job title on the Arabic screen ('Self-check of the job queue', 'Load the daily rate file', 'Clean up finished jobs'), although every row carries titleAr (08-jobs-list-ar.jpg). JobsPage.tsx renders no titleEn cell; the Roles and Sequences screens choose nameAr when the language is Arabic. Search by Arabic text works (attack/ar-check.txt), and the panel title is Arabic.

At the bar volume the screen's 'Enter opens the best match' fails for the main search people will type. 'Self-check of the job queue' matches 24,622 rows, the server sends ranked:false above 10,000 matches (attack/ranked.txt), and Enter only moves focus into the list (kernel/lists/ListView.tsx afterSearchEnter). The builder's comparison driver depends on it and errors 3 of 3 times on the 100,000-job demo, but verified in verify's 2,000-row health check. The newest rows for that search are 3 queued jobs that cannot be re-run, so the user must arrow past them.

Most of the 100,000 seeded jobs are of kinds no module registers (audit.digest, the daily rate file, payment reminders and others). Their panel shows the raw key 'audit.digest (audit.digest)' in both languages, they cannot be re-run even by an administrator (03-seeded-kind-cannot-rerun-en.jpg), and their error text is the generic 'The job stopped with an error. (jobs.seed)'. So the demo shows a list of jobs that mostly cannot be acted on.
Every job panel tells administrators 'Read only: Your roles let you view this record but not change it', which is misleading next to working Run again and Cancel buttons (02, 05, 06 screenshots).

The Schedules list's Kind column shows the raw key (jobs.cleanup, jobs.selfCheck) instead of the kind's name, and the seeded schedule's name is 'Clean up finished jobs / تنظيف المهام المنتهية', both languages in one field (07-schedules-en.jpg).

Keyboard: Ctrl+Enter in the Start a job dialog's JSON field does not start the job; the user must Tab to Start and press Enter. Alt+N, Alt+R and Alt+K work, live progress updates (15% then 30% while running), cancel is immediate, and the output downloads (04, 05, 06 screenshots).

The worker container holds the erp_owner connection string (ConnectionStrings__Owner). erp_owner owns every table and can ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and every future module's job handler will run in that process. A dedicated login role for the worker, holding only the erp_auth switch and the erp_app grants, would shrink the blast radius. No leak was observed: erp_owner is NOBYPASSRLS and RLS is forced.

Audit traceability: work done by scheduled jobs, such as the 50,038 deletions, is recorded with actor_kind 'job' and no actor. Who caused it can only be traced through the correlation id to the job, then to the schedule, then to the schedule's own creation row (attack/planner-audit.txt).

Plant L2 (a job bound to a workspace named in its parameters) passed every static G1 gate and every module test, but was neutralised by design, because a job's work and finish share one transaction bound to its own workspace. Still, no gate exercises the worker's tenant binding (the G1 environment runs no worker).
